findings.title: Individual client/user resources are created without a type
findings.body: `getOrCreateResource` creates the resource via `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId())` and never calls `resource.setType(resourceType)`. The all-resource created in `init` has its type set explicitly via `resource.setType(type)`, but the per-instance resources produced here are stored with a null/empty type. Downstream consumers that filter by type will silently skip them. In particular, `ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission` calls `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, …)`, so it only sees the all-resource (`"Clients"`) and never the individual client resources. The returned set therefore contains only the all-resource name and never any individual client IDs, so callers that filter clients shown to an admin will see no per-client entries. Set the type on the resource in `getOrCreateResource` (e.g. `resource.setType(resourceType)` right after `resourceStore.create`) so that individual resources are discoverable by type.

findings.title: Potential NPE when the all-clients resource does not exist
findings.body: In `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`, when no resource is found by name the code falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)`. That method can legitimately return `null` (it returns null when the schema is not supported, when `resourceType` is null, when the type is not registered, or when the resource is not in the store). The result is then passed to `authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()` without a null check, which will throw a NullPointerException. Add a null check before calling `findByResource` and return false if the all-clients resource is missing.

findings.title: Dead code: getEvaluationContext is never called
findings.body: `ClientPermissionsV2.getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken)` is defined as a private method but is not referenced anywhere in the file. It builds a `DefaultEvaluationContext` with a `kc.client.id` attribute but is never used by `hasPermission`, `hasGrantedPermission`, or any other code path. Either delete it or wire it into the actual evaluation paths that need a client-aware context.

findings.title: getResourceName does not handle the Clients resource type
findings.body: `getResourceName` only has a branch for `USERS_RESOURCE_TYPE`. For a policy whose resource type is `CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE`, the method falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`. The resources created for individual clients by `getOrCreateResource` are named with the client's internal UUID (`resolveClient` returns `client.getId()`), and `getDisplayName()` returns that same UUID. So when an admin views a client-targeted permission in the UI, the resource is shown as the UUID rather than the human-readable client name. Add a `Clients` branch that resolves `resource.getName()` via `session.clients().getClientById(...)` and returns `client.getClientId()` (or the client's display name) for individual resources, and "All clients" for the all-resource, matching the existing `USERS` pattern.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission and per-client filtering are not tested
findings.body: The new `ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission(String)` and the per-client resource lookup path in `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` are not exercised by any test in `PermissionClientTest`. The tests only cover scenarios where the specific resource exists. There is no test that verifies a caller with a per-client scope permission (no all-clients permission) is correctly identified via `getClientsWithPermission`, nor one that exercises the all-clients fallback when a per-client resource exists with a different scope than the one being checked. Adding such tests would have caught the missing `setType` bug.
